canvas-01.description: Lower half of Sheet 1 of the 1925 Cresskill atlas, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points up and to the left. It covers the centre of the borough on both sides of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), whose tracks run diagonally across the sheet with a turntable, coal shed, passenger depot and freight house beside them. East of the line, Railroad Avenue runs along the tracks, and Allen Street and Union Avenue lead east to Willow and Washington Streets and Meadow Street; this is the business block, with stores, a drug store, a hotel, an auto repair shop, the concrete-block garage and the Fire Department and Borough Hall, the Y.M.C.A. and the Congregational Church on Union Avenue. South of Madison Avenue, Mill Street runs south through large, thinly built lots crossed by a brook. West of the railroad, Cresskill Avenue and Grant Avenue meet near a small park, and Madison Avenue runs southwest past the post office, the Merritt Park Gospel Church and the yard of the Cresskill Lumber and Supply Co. with its lumber sheds, to Munroe Avenue (marked not opened), Waverly Place and the platted but unbuilt blocks on 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets. Tenakill Brook crosses the southwest corner. A small locator map of New Jersey, the sheet's key to symbols and the scale bar are printed on the sheet; the upper half (title, index and key map at 1000 ft to an inch) is not part of this map.
notes: Railroad Avenue is now Piermont Road; its junctions were left out of the fit (5 to 7 m residuals, the modern road no longer follows the old line beside the tracks).
Meadow Street is now Spring Street; Mill Street is now Milton Street; Munroe Avenue is now Monroe Avenue.
Madison Avenue east of the railroad is now East Madison Avenue.
Allen Street today meets Union Avenue west of Willow Street; on the sheet it reaches Union Avenue east of Willow (junction excluded).
Cresskill Lumber and Supply Co. yard with night watchman and clock; post office and passenger depot beside the railroad.
Munroe Avenue is marked not opened.

Sheet 1. Upper half: title cartouche, water and fire department notes, specials index and key map of the borough at 1000 ft to an inch (not configured). Lower half: map at 100 ft to an inch of the business district at the Northern Railroad of New Jersey: Union Av, Allen St, Railroad Av (now Piermont Road), Willow, Washington, Meadow (now Spring Street), Mill (now Milton Street), Madison Av, Cresskill Av, Grant Av, Munroe and Waverly Pl. One configured part (lower half); a small state locator map at upper left of the lower half is masked out. Drawn turned on the page, north about -31 degrees.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the 1925 Cresskill atlas, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north up, covers the northwest of the borough between Jefferson Avenue and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), which runs down the east edge. Grant Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the northwest to Cresskill Avenue. North of it is a recent residential subdivision laid out with rounded block corners: Mezzine Drive loops around blocks on Brookside Avenue, Harvard Place and Concord Place, closed on the south by Bergen Terrace and Gilmore Avenue. Most of its lots are still empty, with scattered frame dwellings and garages, chiefly along Brookside Avenue and the west side of Mezzine Drive. Tenakill Brook runs south through the middle of the sheet, with the old meander of the brook shown by a dashed line beside the subdivision, and a second brook branches east toward the railroad across a large open lot. South of Grant Avenue the land is mostly open: Orchard Street runs south past the Cresskill Public School (brick, heated by hot water) to Prospect Avenue; in the southeast corner small blocks on Grant Avenue, Cresskill Avenue and Cottage Place carry a dozen dwellings. Along the south edge a strip of narrow, platted lots lies between Prospect and Munroe Avenues and Waverly Place, mostly unbuilt; the end of Munroe Avenue is marked not opened. A water main runs along Grant and Cresskill Avenues.
notes: Orchard (south of Grant Avenue) is now part of Brookside Avenue; Harvard Place is now Harvard Street; Concord Place is now the north end of Gilmore Avenue; Munroe Avenue is now Monroe Avenue.
The east loop of Mezzine Drive and Bergen Terrace east of Gilmore Avenue are not in the modern street data.
Modern Jefferson Avenue continues north through what is open block 13 here, to Grant Avenue and the west loop of Mezzine Drive (now Merrifield Way); that junction was excluded.
Cresskill Public School on Orchard Street.

Sheet 2, 100 ft to an inch, north up. Northwest residential area: Grant Av, Brookside Av, Orchard (now the south end of Brookside Avenue), Mezzine Drive, Harvard Pl (now Harvard Street), Concord Pl (now the north end of Gilmore Avenue), Gilmore Av, Bergen Ter, Cresskill Av, Cottage Pl, Prospect Av, Munroe Av, Waverly Pl, Jefferson Av; Tenakill Brook; Cresskill Public School; railroad at the east edge. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the 1925 Cresskill atlas, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north up, covers the southwest of the borough, a regular grid platted in small 25 ft lots. Munroe Avenue runs along the top edge, Madison, Magnolia and Evergreen Avenues cross the sheet east to west, and 9th, 8th, Jefferson, 7th, 6th, 5th, 4th and 3rd Streets run north to south, with Jefferson Avenue bent slightly where it crosses the grid. In the southwest a smaller grid of short streets lies west of Jefferson Avenue: two Private Streets, Elm and Chestnut Streets and Cedar Street, and east of Jefferson the short Maple and Oak Streets. Building is thin and scattered: one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, a few poultry houses and stables, concentrated near Madison and Magnolia Avenues and along Jefferson Avenue; most lots, especially south of Evergreen Avenue, are empty. The main institution is St. Theresa's Roman Catholic Church on Munroe Avenue, with steam heat and electric light; a large open tract (block 14) lies in the northwest corner and large unplatted lots in the south. Water mains run along Madison and Magnolia Avenues and Jefferson Avenue.
notes: The northern Private Street is now Smith Terrace and the southern one Glenview Terrace; Oak Street is now Sycamore Street; Elm Street is now Poplar Street; Orchard Street is now Brookside Avenue; Munroe Avenue is now Monroe Avenue.
Maple Street (between Jefferson Avenue and 7th Street) is not in the modern street data.
Jefferson Avenue is drawn about 35 ft wide against about 50 ft between today's parcels.
St. Theresa R.C. Church on Munroe Avenue.

Sheet 3, 100 ft to an inch, north up. Southwest grid: Munroe, Madison, Magnolia and Evergreen Avs, 3rd to 9th Streets and Jefferson Av; Private St (two, now Smith Terrace and Glenview Terrace), Maple St, Oak (now Sycamore Street), Elm (now Poplar Street), Chestnut, Cedar. St. Theresa R.C. Church. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: Main map of Sheet 4 of the 1925 Cresskill atlas, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points up and to the left. It covers the east side of the borough from the Demarest borough line along the top edge south to Madison Avenue and Huylers Dock Road. County Road runs down the west edge and then southeast to Madison Avenue; Westervelt Avenue and Hillside Avenue cross the sheet from it toward the east, where Hillside Avenue turns north and Lamb's Lane leaves to the east at a small triangle (block 77). South of Hillside Avenue, New Street, Center Street and Oak Street enclose large blocks platted in long rows of narrow lots, nearly all still empty. The built-up part is along Westervelt and Hillside Avenues, with a row of one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages, and at the west edge, where Union Avenue and Meadow Street meet County Road: here stand a concrete-block garage and repair shop with a gasoline station, a plumbing shop and a few brick-tile dwellings. North of Westervelt Avenue lies a large open tract (block 72) crossed by a brook and a right of way, partly covered by the inset of part 2. Water mains run along County Road, Westervelt Avenue and Hillside Avenue.
notes: Westervelt Avenue is now Westervelt Place; Meadow Street is now Spring Street; Madison Avenue is now East Madison Avenue.
The short stretch of Hillside Avenue east of the triangle at Lamb's Lane is now Engle Street.
Concrete-block garage and repair shop with gasoline station at Union Avenue and County Road; one tile dwelling marked as drawn from plans.
The heavy-lined box at the top of the sheet is an inset (part 2) drawn over block 72; it does not show the ground beneath it.

Sheet 4, 100 ft to an inch (entire sheet), turned on the page with north about -34 degrees. East side: County Rd, Westervelt Av (now Westervelt Place), Hillside Av, Union Av, Meadow (now Spring Street), New St, Center St, Oak St, Madison Av (now East Madison Avenue), Lambs Lane, Huylers Dock Rd. Two parts: part 1 the main map; part 2 an inset framed by a heavy line at the top, showing block 71 at South Street and County Road (west of County Road, drawn over the open lots of block 72).

sheet-4-2.description: Inset at the top of Sheet 4 of the 1925 Cresskill atlas, framed by a heavy line and drawn over the open lots of block 72 at the same scale (100 ft to an inch) and orientation as the rest of the sheet, with north up and to the left. It shows the northeast corner of block 71, which lies west of County Road and south of South Street and falls off the edge of the main map: South Street along the top, here the boundary between the Borough of Demarest and the Borough of Cresskill, and County Road on the right with a 12 inch water main and a hydrant. Five narrow lots (15 to 19) face South Street, four of them with one- or two-storey frame dwellings; a further dwelling with a garage stands in the middle of the block. The rest of the inset is empty. The sheet's north arrow is drawn across the inset's left frame.
notes: Placed on one hand-picked junction (County Road / South Street) and a point derived from it 300 ft down County Road at the scale and rotation of part 1; low confidence.
The borough line between Demarest and Cresskill runs along South Street.

Sheet 4, 100 ft to an inch (entire sheet), turned on the page with north about -34 degrees. East side: County Rd, Westervelt Av (now Westervelt Place), Hillside Av, Union Av, Meadow (now Spring Street), New St, Center St, Oak St, Madison Av (now East Madison Avenue), Lambs Lane, Huylers Dock Rd. Two parts: part 1 the main map; part 2 an inset framed by a heavy line at the top, showing block 71 at South Street and County Road (west of County Road, drawn over the open lots of block 72).
